claim_verdicts.evidence: Carried from round 1 (old claim 1, unchanged). Pod lifecycle: "If the readiness probe returns a failed state, the EndpointSlice controller removes the Pod's IP address from the EndpointSlices of all Services that match the Pod." Ready: "the Pod is able to serve requests and should be added to the load balancing pools of all matching Services." Deployment: "the Deployment gradually scales it up while scaling down the old ReplicaSet".

Text now equals round-1 suggested_text. Deployment docs: "when you roll back to an earlier revision, only the Deployment's Pod template part is rolled back"; a template change is a rollout: "A new ReplicaSet is created, and the Deployment gradually scales it up while scaling down the old ReplicaSet". blue-green.txt line 23: the same 2 Pods, none restarted.

Carried from round 1 (old claim 3, unchanged). api-green.yaml: name api-green, replicas: 2, matchLabels/template label app: api-green; Service api-green selector app: api-green, port 8080. base/api.yaml replicas: 2. Output: api 2 2, api-green 2 2.

Carried from round 1 (old claim 4, unchanged). Service docs: "The set of Pods targeted by a Service is usually determined by a selector that you define." "The controller for that Service continuously scans for Pods that match its selector". Service api selects app: api; green's Pods carry only app: api-green.

Gateway API traffic splitting: "`weight` is an optional parameter and if not specified, defaults to 1." "If only a single backend is specified for a route rule it implicitly receives 100% of the traffic". set_backends api-green writes no weight (release.sh 151-159), so route_backends prints weight 1. Section 4 now rests on this rule instead of Traefik behaviour.
